name: Legal's mate idea
m: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 Bc4 Bg4 Nc3 g6 Nxe5 Bxd1 Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5#

n.7: Too slow. Black spends a move on the kingside while the g4-bishop's pin on f3 is only an illusion.
n.8: Breaks the pin! The knight takes e5 and offers the queen, because Bxf7+ and Nd5 are coming.
n.9: Greed. Taking the queen walks into mate. Black had to accept a worse position with ...dxe5 Qxg4.
n.10: Check from the bishop; the king has only e7.
n.12: Checkmate: the knights and bishop cover every square. Lesson: a pinned knight isn't really pinned if the queen sacrifice leads to mate.

name: Blackburne Shilling: 3...Nd4
m: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxd4 exd4 O-O

n.5: A trick move: it hopes for 4.Nxe5?? Qg5!, which wins a lot. It moves the same knight twice and gives up e5's defence.
n.6: Calm and strong: just take the knight. Don't grab e5 with Nxe5, that's exactly the trap.
n.8: Castle and keep developing: c3 or Re1 come next, and the d4-pawn becomes a target.

name: Greedy ...b5 in the Queen's Gambit Accepted
m: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 c6 axb5 cxb5 Qf3

n.5: Trying to hold the c4-pawn with ...b5 is a classic mistake: it leaves a8 and the long diagonal loose.
n.6: Strikes at the b5-pawn right away.
n.8: Opens the a-file toward the a8-rook.
n.10: The double attack on a8 down the long diagonal (and the rook on a1 down the a-file) wins material: Black can't cover both.

name: Elephant Trap
m: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 cxd5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxd5 Bxd8 Bb4+ Qd2 Bxd2+ Kxd2 Kxd8

n.10: White thinks the f6-knight is pinned and grabs d5. It isn't really pinned: Black has a trick.
n.11: Take back! Give up the queen for a moment.
n.13: Check! The bishop forces White to give the queen back.
n.14: White must block with the queen.
n.17: Black recaptures the bishop and comes out a knight for a pawn ahead. Remember: a pin against the queen can be broken if you win the queen back with check.

name: Exchange Ruy trap: 6.Nxe5?
m: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 Bc5 Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5 Qd4

n.10: Looks like it wins a pawn, but the knight on e5 and the f2-pawn are both loose.
n.11: A double attack: the queen hits the e5-knight and, with the c5-bishop, threatens ...Qxf2 mate. White can't meet both threats and loses the knight back with interest.

name: The ...Nxd4 pin trick
m: Nf3 Nc6 d4 d5 c4 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd4 Qxd4 Bxf3 gxf3

n.7: Black hopes for Nxd4?? Bxd1, using the pin on the f3-knight. But the pin doesn't matter if you take with the queen.
n.8: Take with the queen! The g4-bishop can win the f3-knight, but White stays a piece up.
n.9: Black takes the knight to break the centre.
n.10: Recapture. White is a piece up; the doubled f-pawns don't matter.

name: Long-diagonal trick ...Nxd4
m: Nf3 c5 c4 Nc6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 d4 Nxd4 exd4 cxd4 Nxd4

n.9: Black counts on the g7-bishop's pressure down the long diagonal. It doesn't add up.
n.11: Black wins a second pawn and attacks c3.
n.12: Take back. The d4-knight is defended by the queen, so ...Bxd4 Qxd4 just leaves White a piece for two pawns up.

name: Poisoned b2-pawn
m: d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Nc3 Qxb2 Nxd5

n.7: Grabbing b2 with the queen is a common mistake: she is far from home and your pieces gain time against her.
n.8: Take the centre pawn with a threat: Nc7+ forks king and rook, and Rb1 can hunt the queen. Black is already in big trouble.

name: The ...Nxd4 queen-trade trick
m: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nd2 Qb6 Qb3 Nxd4 exd4 cxd4 Qxb6 axb6 cxd4

n.11: Black hopes the open c-file and queen trade make up for the knight. They don't.
n.13: Black takes back a pawn and pressures c3.
n.14: Trade queens first, so Black has no ...Qxb3 tricks.
n.16: White has an extra piece for a pawn; keep it simple and develop.

name: The fork trick fails: ...Nxe4
m: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 Bc5 c3 Nxe4 dxe4

n.9: Black hopes for a fork trick, but with d3 played the e4-pawn is defended.
n.10: Just take. With d3 played, e4 was defended all along, and Black has no good follow-up. White is a full knight up for a pawn.

name: The ...Bxf2+ shot fails
m: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Nxc6 Bxf2+ Kxf2 bxc6

n.9: A tempting check, but it just gives up a bishop for a pawn.
n.10: Take the bishop. Your king is safe enough; there's no follow-up for Black.
n.11: Black recaptures the knight, but White is a piece up for a pawn.

name: 4...dxe4? loses a piece
m: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5 dxe4 exf6

n.7: Natural-looking, but it ignores the attack on the f6-knight.
n.8: Take the knight! The e5-pawn was attacking it. Black can win the e4-pawn back but stays a piece down for a pawn.

name: 4...dxc4? loses the knight
m: c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e4 d5 e5 dxc4 exf6

n.7: Black grabs a pawn and forgets the knight on f6 is attacked.
n.8: Take the knight. Black gets a pawn, White gets a whole piece.

name: 3.Nxd5? loses a knight
m: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nxd5 cxd5 exd5 Qxd5

n.5: Take the knight with the pawn.
n.7: Recapture. Black is a piece up for a pawn and the queen is safe on d5.

name: 6.Bb5+?? hangs the bishop
m: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5 exd5 Qxd5 Ngf3 cxd4 Bb5+ Qxb5

n.10: A reflex check, but the queen on d5 covers b5 along the rank.
n.11: Just take it. Always check what your queen already sees.

name: 4.Bb5+?? hangs the bishop
m: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nf3 Nf6 Bb5+ Qxb5

n.6: A common reflex check. But the queen on d5 sees b5.
n.7: Take it for free. In the Scandinavian, always look at what your early queen controls.
